item.title: Irish rugby sevens star Harry McNulty returns for 2027 Coral Coast Fiji 7s
item.description: Irish Rugby 7s star Harry McNulty will return to Fiji for the 2027 McDonald's Coral Coast Fiji 7s, where he will once again represent the McDonald's Mike Friday Select 7s. McNulty's return adds further international experience to the invitational side as legendary coach Mike Friday prepares his team for a third consecutive campaign at the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Irish Rugby 7s star Harry McNulty will return to Fiji for the 2027 McDonald's Coral Coast Fiji 7s, where he will once again represent the McDonald's Mike Friday Select 7s.

McNulty's return adds further international experience to the invitational side as legendary coach Mike Friday prepares his team for a third consecutive campaign at the tournament.

Known for his physical presence, powerful running and competitive spirit, McNulty has represented Ireland on the international stage, including at the Olympic Games.

He joins a strong line-up of international players already confirmed for the 2027 Select 7s squad.

The team includes South African stars Rosko "Specmagic" Specman, Branco du Preez and Justin Geduld, French Rugby 7s legend Terry Bouhraoua and Australian player Pama Fou.

The 15th annual McDonald's Coral Coast Fiji 7s will be held at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka from the 14th to the 16th of January, 2027.

item.title: Fiji fall 43-15 to Ireland in Dublin
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians suffered a 43-15 defeat to Ireland in Dublin in the Nations Championship after the Ireland produced a dominant second-half performance, scoring several unanswered tries to pull away from the Flying Fijians. Fiji captain Tevita Ikanivere says the team made a promising start but Ireland fought back and capitalised on their opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians suffered a 43-15 defeat to Ireland in Dublin in the Nations Championship after the Ireland produced a dominant second-half performance, scoring several unanswered tries to pull away from the Flying Fijians.

Fiji captain Tevita Ikanivere says the team made a promising start but Ireland fought back and capitalised on their opportunities.

Ikanivere says Fiji needs to prepare better for its next match, adding that the players have learnt a lot under the new coach.

He says Ireland took its chances and never backed down, describing the match as an important learning experience for the team.

Meanwhile, Fiji started with attacking intent, with Josua Tuisova and captain Peceli Yato scoring tries to give the Flying Fijians an early lead.

Ireland opened the scoring through Tommy O’Brien in the eighth minute, with the conversion successful to give the hosts a 7-0 lead.

Tuisova responded in the 19th minute, scoring following a lineout inside Ireland's 22-metre area.

Ben Volavola missed the conversion, leaving Fiji trailing 7-5.

Fiji then took the lead when Wainiqolo made a strong break and offloaded to Yato, who crossed for the team's second try. Volavola converted to put Fiji ahead 12-7.

Ireland fought back through two first-half tries from Robert Baloucoune to take a 17-12 lead.

However, Fiji reduced the deficit through a successful penalty from Volavola after Ireland captain James Ryan received a yellow card, leaving the half-time score at 17-15.

The second half proved difficult for Fiji as Ireland increased its attacking pressure and took control of the match.

Ireland extended its lead with a converted try in the 46th minute to make it 22-15.

The match also saw a concerning incident when Ireland's debutant James McNabney was knocked unconscious following head contact near Fiji's try line.

Fiji's Inoke Ravuiwasa received a yellow card during the incident.

Ireland continued to capitalise on its opportunities, with Andrew Porter scoring in the 54th minute before Tommy O’Brien added another try in the 60th minute.

Both conversions were successful, extending Ireland's lead to 36-15.

Fiji had opportunities to get back into the match but struggled to finish its attacking movements.

Luke Tagi appeared to score following a lineout, but the try was ruled out due to a knock-on, while Ikanivere also lost control of the ball just before reaching Ireland's try line.

Ireland added another try through Nick Timoney in the 77th minute, with the conversion successful to extend the score to 43-15.

Wainiqolo made one final attempt towards Ireland's try line in the closing stages but dropped the ball just short of the scoring line.

Ireland captain Tadhg Beirne says his side had to work hard for the victory, acknowledging that playing against the Flying Fijians was not easy.

Fiji will face Italy in their next match next Sunday at 4.40am at Bluenergy Stadium in Udine, Italy.

item.title: Nadroga beats Ra to claim Farebrother Sullivan Trophy
item.description: An electric atmosphere filled Narauyaba Ground in Rakiraki as approximately 12,000 spectators gathered to witness Nadroga successfully claim the Inkk Farebrother Sullivan Trophy with a hard-fought 28-20 victory over Ra. Nadroga got off to a strong start, scoring the opening try in the third minute through their blindside flanker to take an early 5-0 lead.
item.content:encoded:
An electric atmosphere filled Narauyaba Ground in Rakiraki as approximately 12,000 spectators gathered to witness Nadroga successfully claim the Inkk Farebrother Sullivan Trophy with a hard-fought 28-20 victory over Ra.

Nadroga got off to a strong start, scoring the opening try in the third minute through their blindside flanker to take an early 5-0 lead.

However, Nadroga were shown a yellow card in the 10th minute after deliberately knocking the ball out of the hands of Ra scrum-half Peni Matawalu.

Ra dominated possession during the first 30 minutes and turned that pressure into points in the 17th minute when their outside centre crossed the try line to level the scores at 5-5.

Nadroga continued to surrender possession through ill-discipline and were shown a second yellow card, this time to their prop.

Despite the setbacks, Nadroga regained the lead with three minutes remaining in the first half, scoring their second try through a powerful driving maul from a lineout to extend their advantage to 10-5.

Nadroga started the second half strongly, scoring their third try in the 44th minute through their blindside winger.

Ra were awarded a penalty in the 49th minute, which their fullback successfully converted to reduce the deficit to 15-8.

Nadroga responded with another try in the 55th minute through their loose forward, extending their lead to 20-8 .

They continued to dominate the scoreboard, scoring their fourth try in the 68th minute to stretch their advantage to 25-8 .

Ra refused to give up, responding with a try through their winger before their prop crossed the try line for another, narrowing the deficit to 20-25 and putting pressure on the defending champions.

However, a late penalty awarded to Nadroga gave them the opportunity to seal the victory.

They opted to kick for goal, successfully extending their lead to secure a 28-20 win.
